instruction: In this empty flowgraph, build a sync-word detector for a test bit stream. Use a repeating Vector Source to play this 64-bit pattern, one sample per bit, leftmost bit first, repeated for as long as the flowgraph runs (the spaces only group the bits): 0011 0110 1110 1011 0010 0001 1000 1001 1111 0001 1110 1011 0110 0001 1100 0010. Record the bit stream in a File Sink with the file name bits.dat and item type float, as 0.0 for a 0 bit and 1.0 for a 1 bit. The pattern contains the 16-bit sync word 1110 1011 0010 0001 once, and also a copy of it with one wrong bit. Detect the sync word with no bit errors allowed, computing the detection inside the flowgraph from the bit stream (do not store the expected result as a fixed pattern). Write the result to a second File Sink with the file name flags.dat and item type float: one sample per input bit, exactly 1.0 on the bit that completes an error-free sync word (its last bit) and exactly 0.0 on every other bit, so the copy with the wrong bit is never marked. Both files must start with the first bit of the pattern, with no delay between them. The sample rate does not affect the result, so you can leave the samp_rate variable as it is. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.
observation: the float samples written to the File Sinks whose file names are bits.dat and flags.dat (item type float)
oracle_checks: main:equal_prefix@bits; main:equal_prefix@bits; main:equal_prefix@flags; main:equal_prefix@flags; main:graph:path
gates: PASS mutation=ok, size=ok, solvability=ok, start_fails=ok, variants=ok
known_limits: Re-themed in round 1 (fix plan 18 Oct, group G1): old dev-01 (16 dB tone gain) shared the {tone} cell with gbf-test-04, which keeps it. The planned block, Correlate Access Code - Bit (digital_correlate_access_code_bb, data bit + 2 x flag per byte), is not in the pinned GNU Radio 3.10.12 GRC catalog (probe access_code_bb_block fails V2), so the item uses the planner's listed alternative (FIR correlator + threshold) with a float 0/1 flag output; the v2 cell is data_source|filter|nonlinear (dev; the planner's pre-check listed it as dev and unused). bits.dat is a second observation point so the stated input pattern is checked. Graph check (round 2): a path from a Vector Source through a block with memory (a filter, a Delay, a correlator block or an Embedded Python block) to a File Sink. A flag depends on 16 bits at different times, so every design that computes it from the bit stream has such a block on the path, including delay-line correlators built from Delay blocks with Add/Subtract, Multiply or byte NOT/AND. Stateless blocks (Add, Multiply, AND, Threshold, ...) are not in the list on purpose: with them, the bit stream multiplied by a stored copy of the expected flags would pass (probe stored_flags_times_bits). Known limits: (1) a deliberate cheat that routes a hard-coded flags pattern through a block with memory (e.g. a one-tap FIR or a Delay of 0) passes the path check; (2) 'do not limit the number of samples' is enforced only as V4 liveness (4096 items at both points); (3) samples 192-3903 are not compared (a periodic source cannot deviate there without also failing the late window or the slip check, but an adversarial time-varying design could); (4) the stream holds one near-miss copy (bit 9 wrong), so a detector that checks only part of the word including bit 9 (e.g. only its last 7 bits, which occur nowhere else in the pattern) writes the same flags. The flags must be exactly 0.0 and 1.0 (stated in the instruction): an FFT correlator whose rounding (about 1e-6) reaches flags.dat through arithmetic (Add Const + Rail) fails (probe fft_correlator_rail_inexact), while an FFT correlator followed by a Threshold (v2) or a Binary Slicer writes exact flags. A Rational Resampler at 1:1 outputs its window 15 samples early, so it needs a Delay of 15 (probes rational_resampler_unaligned and rational_resampler_delay). Relation to gbf-dev-03 (same fixer group): both filter float data, but dev-03 is a symbol-length rectangular matched filter on +-1 NRZ samples at 8 samples per symbol (modify), while this item detects a specific 16-bit word in a 1-sample-per-bit 0/1 stream with a decision threshold (build). Shipped variants use a Threshold with hysteresis, a +-1 mapping, a byte source, or a Rail clamp as the decision stage (v4), all in the dev cell. Correct alternatives whose v2 cell differs are kept as passing probes in build.py (--probes); their v2 signatures, for the reserved-signature step (R1/R2): binary_slicer_threshold: data_source|filter|linear_demod (test); delay_line_add_sub: combine|data_source|delay|nonlinear (test); delay_line_product: data_source|delay|multiply (test); delay_line_bitwise_bytes: data_source|delay|nonlinear (test); rational_resampler_delay: data_source|delay|filter|nonlinear (train); embedded_python: custom|data_source (dev). Those that hash to train are also shipped as variants (v5 onwards), so the reserved list includes them. The Embedded Python cell custom|data_source is also the cell of gbf-dev-03's Embedded Python alternative; both items are dev.

instruction: In this flowgraph, simulate the amplitude of a Rayleigh flat-fading channel at a sample rate of 48 kHz. Generate complex Gaussian noise with an RMS magnitude of 0.8 (the square root of the mean of |z|^2 over its samples z is 0.8), take the magnitude of every sample, and write the magnitudes as float samples to a File Sink whose file name is envelope.dat. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples. Like any Rayleigh envelope with that RMS, the samples in envelope.dat must have an RMS level of 0.8 and a mean of 0.709 (0.8 times the square root of pi, divided by 2), each within 3 %.
observation: the float samples written to the File Sink whose file name is envelope.dat
oracle_checks: main:rms@env; main:mean@env; main:graph:path; main:graph:block_present
gates: PASS mutation=ok, size=ok, solvability=ok, start_fails=ok, variants=ok
known_limits: Re-themed on 18 Oct (fix plan): the former band-limited-noise item was a template twin of gbf-test-03. Known oracle limits (drafted by Claude; for the team). (1) Only the first two moments of the envelope are checked (there is no distribution feature): the mean/RMS pair (ratio 0.886) rejects the power |z|^2, a single real component (half-normal, mean -10 %), uniform complex noise and constants, but a non-Gaussian source with the same two moments would pass. GNU Radio's complex Laplacian and impulse noise types fail at run time ('invalid type'), so no noise-type graph check is used. (2) The path check proves that the File Sink is fed from a noise generator; it accepts Noise Source, Fast Noise Source and the AWGN of Channel Model / Channel Model 2 / Dynamic Channel Model. A sum-of-sinusoids Fading Model fed by a constant is not complex Gaussian noise as the instruction asks and fails it (probe fading_model_jakes); a deterministic signal added on a noise path could pass. (3) The 48 kHz sample rate is unobservable in white-noise statistics and is checked as a variable's value (block_present variable value 48000; numeric comparison, so 48e3 passes, an expression such as 48*1000 does not: probe samp_rate_expression). The harness's empty start graph already holds samp_rate = 48000, so this fails only an answer that rewrites or removes it. (4) The noise seed is not specified (the reference keeps seed 42 so gate runs are bit-identical; GNU Radio's seed 0 is also fixed). The stated 3 % is >= 5 sigma from every valid generator over 300 seeds (Noise Source within 0.62 %, default Fast Noise Source within 1.9 %, Channel Model AWGN within 1.3 %); a Fast Noise Source whose pool is shrunk far below its 8192-variate default can miss it on some seeds. (5) A Head block larger than the 65536-item capture is not detected. Variant signatures (v2): v1, v2 envelope|noise (dev); v3 envelope|noise|nonlinear (hashes to train) and v4 channel_model|envelope (hashes to test; no test task uses that cell) are genuine structural alternatives (|z|^2 then a square root; a Channel Model's AWGN) and belong on the reserved list (fix_plan R1/R2); probe complex_to_magphase (other:blocks_complex_to_magphase|noise) also passes.

instruction: This flowgraph plays a repeating NRZ test pattern: a Vector Source sends +1/-1 symbols as rectangular pulses, 8 samples per symbol (4 kBd at 32 kHz), through a Throttle to a File Sink that writes nrz.dat. Add a matched filter for these rectangular pulses and write its output to a new File Sink with the file name mf.dat and item type float. For every input sample the filter output must be the average of that sample and the 7 samples before it (one symbol), so that it reaches exactly +1 or -1 at the end of every full symbol. Keep one output sample per input sample, aligned with the input (no decimation and no extra delay). Each output value must be within 0.001 of that average; the first 7 output samples, while the filter fills, do not matter. Keep nrz.dat exactly as it is. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.
observation: the float samples written to the File Sinks whose file names are mf.dat and nrz.dat (item type float)

known_limits: Re-themed in round 1 (fix plan 18 Oct, group G1): old dev-03 (retune a unipolar tone) was a template twin of gbf-test-04 ({tone}, kept by test-04) and in substance a parameter-tune item (round-1 F1); the new task is a genuine structural modify (a block is added). Oracle: exact equality was not used because an FFT filter (accepted by the plan's graph check) is correct but not bit-identical; corr_ref + rms + 1/8-lattice imply the stated 0.001 tolerance over samples 7-390, and the lattice/min/max checks cover the whole capture. Margins of typical wrong outputs over the corr window: length 7: corr 0.9924, rms ratio 0.902; length 9: corr 0.9930, rms ratio 1.089; delay 1: corr 0.9767, rms ratio 1.000; scale 0.12: corr 1.0000, rms ratio 0.960; no filter: corr 0.6862, rms ratio 1.220 (thresholds: corr >= 0.99999, rms within 0.1%). Known limits: (1) the path check accepts any of the listed filter blocks (and Add, for delay-line designs) between a Vector Source and a File Sink, so a deliberate cheat that routes a hard-coded output through a one-tap filter or an Add would pass; (2) 'do not limit the number of samples' is enforced only as V4 liveness (4096 items at both points); (3) samples 391-4095 are checked for the 1/8 lattice and the +-1 range, not exactly. Concept relations: gbf-test-13 shapes NRZ data for transmission (low-pass interpolation x8), the receive-side counterpart; gbf-dev-01 (same fixer group) correlates a 0/1 bit stream with a 16-bit sync word and thresholds it (build), this item averages +-1 NRZ samples over one symbol (modify). Training spec t19 (RSSI meter) also uses a Moving Average, for level metering. Variant signatures for the reserved-signature step (R1/R2): v1-v3 share the reference cell data_source|filter (dev); v4 (delay line + Add + Multiply Const) is combine|data_source|delay, which hashes to train, and is shipped so the reserved list includes it. The Embedded Python alternative (custom|data_source) is dev.

instruction:
This flowgraph is a heterodyne mixer that converts a radio-frequency (RF) test carrier down to an intermediate frequency (IF). It runs at a sample rate of 48 kHz. The Signal Source block rf generates the RF carrier, a 10.7 kHz cosine with amplitude 0.8 (float samples). A second Signal Source, the local oscillator (amplitude 1), is multiplied with the carrier, and a low-pass filter after the multiplier keeps only the difference frequency. The result goes to the File Sink whose file name is if.dat (item type float).

At the moment GNU Radio Companion refuses to generate the flowgraph: validation reports that a parameter value cannot be evaluated.

Please repair it so that if.dat receives the RF carrier converted to a 2 kHz IF: a 2 kHz tone (within 1 %) with amplitude 0.4, which is half the RF amplitude, as an ideal multiplier with a unit-amplitude local oscillator gives (an RMS of 0.283, within 5 %). Everything else in the output, in particular the multiplier's sum-frequency product, must be at least 40 dB weaker than the IF tone. These figures apply after the first 4096 output samples, which cover the filter's start-up. Keep the mixer structure (the RF source and the local oscillator feeding the multiplier, then a low-pass filter, then the File Sink if.dat), and keep the RF source rf unchanged. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.
observation: 'out': the float samples written to the File Sink whose file name is if.dat (item type float); 'rf': the output of the Signal Source block rf (edge tap, no extra block). Both keep producing samples (V4 liveness: 16384 items at each point).

known_limits: Re-themed on 18 Oct 2026 (fix plan): the old dev-04 (500 Hz tone + 60 Hz hum, high-pass) was a template twin of the old gbf-test-05 and hashed to train under signature v2; both were re-themed. Known limits: (1) the mixer-structure graph checks are by block type, so an answer that parks rf on a sink and mixes a different source into if.dat would pass them; (2) the LPF cutoff and width are not requirements (a repair may also retune or replace the filter, as long as the stated output holds); (3) an LO at 35.3 kHz (the alias of 12.7 kHz at 48 kHz) produces identical samples and passes; (4) the 40 dB purity requirement is measured as the power outside 1.9-2.1 kHz (band_fraction >= 0.9999, Blackman window since review round 2, so an IF anywhere within the stated 1 % passes; variant v5 and build.py --probes cover off-grid IFs); a spur within 100 Hz of the IF would count as IF power. Level L1 under the proposed rule R7 (5 functional blocks, single rate; a mixer is not a modulator); the team confirms R7. Relation to gbf-test-18 (CW receiver: complex down-conversion, decimation, BFO) and gbf-dev-06 (SSB mixing) is conceptual only. L1 repair conventions shared with gbf-test-10: symptom-only wording, p2p = properties of the parts the fault does not touch (R8), an edge observation point on the kept source. Signature-v2 cells of the variants: v1_high_side_lo: filter|mix|tone; v2_literal_swapped_throttle: filter|mix|tone; v3_parameter_block_fir: filter|mix|tone; v4_expression_variables: filter|mix|tone; v5_lo_within_tolerance: filter|mix|tone.

instruction: This flowgraph models an amplifier that saturates: Gaussian noise goes through a limiter (the Rail block), and two File Sinks record the noise entering the limiter (noise_in.dat) and the limiter's output (limited.dat) as float samples. Retune it for a new operating point. The noise entering the limiter must stay Gaussian and get a standard deviation of 0.4; measured on noise_in.dat, it must be within 2 % of 0.4. The limiter must clip symmetrically: its upper clip level must be the level that Gaussian noise with a standard deviation of exactly 0.4 exceeds 2.5 % of the time, and its lower clip level the level it falls below 2.5 % of the time, so that on average 5 % of the samples are clipped. Each clip level must be within 1 % of that exact value. Change parameter values only: do not add, remove or rewire any blocks, and do not add, remove or rename variables. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.
observation: the float samples written to the File Sinks whose file names are noise_in.dat (the limiter's input) and limited.dat (the limiter's output)
oracle_checks: f2p:rms@noise; f2p:max@out; f2p:min@out; p2p:graph:block_present; p2p:graph:same_blocks_as_start; p2p:graph:same_connections_as_start

known_limits: Re-themed on 18 Oct (fix plan): the former harmonic multiplier was in the square-to-sine group (filter|harmonic_wave, train) and a template twin of gbf-test-12. Known oracle limits (drafted by Claude; for the team). (1) The clipped share (5 %) is not measured directly (there is no distribution feature): it follows from the measured noise standard deviation (P1, 2 %) and the clip levels (P2, 1 %), which the Rail's exact limiting makes measurable without estimation error, plus the Gaussian check (P4). Within the stated tolerances the share is about 4.3-5.7 %; in practice the amplitude is the standard deviation exactly and the instruction ties each clip level to standard deviation exactly 0.4, so the clip-level tolerance alone decides (4.77-5.22 % clipped). (2) 'Stay Gaussian' is checked on the noise_type parameter (GRC's writer exports every parameter, so the harness's final graph carries it; the compact files keep it explicitly). (3) Value-only is enforced with same_blocks_as_start (variables value_only: no variable may be added, removed or renamed, as the instruction says) and same_connections_as_start (isomorphic; block instances may be renamed); probes helper_variable, renamed_variable and rewired_same_blocks fail; renamed_blocks and variant v4 pass. (4) The noise seed and the sample rate are free (unobservable in white-noise statistics; not mentioned in the instruction). Distinct from gbf-dev-02 (build: Rayleigh envelope of complex noise) and gbf-test-03 (build: band-limited noise). Variant signatures (v2): all noise|nonlinear (dev).

instruction: In this empty flowgraph, build a test bench for a single-sideband (SSB) transmitter that uses the phasing method. Set samp_rate to 48 kHz; this is the sample rate of the SSB output. First make a two-tone audio test signal at an audio sample rate of 8 kHz: the sum of a 700 Hz sinusoid with amplitude 0.4 and a 2.4 kHz sinusoid with amplitude 0.25 (float samples). Write this audio to a File Sink with the file name audio.dat (float items, 8 kHz). Then turn this audio into an upper-sideband (USB) signal on a 10 kHz carrier at 48 kHz by the phasing method: use GNU Radio's Hilbert block to form the analytic (complex) signal of the audio, and shift that up to the carrier. Write the result as a real signal to a File Sink with the file name ssb.dat (float items, 48 kHz). In ssb.dat the 700 Hz tone must appear at 10.7 kHz with amplitude 0.4 and the 2.4 kHz tone at 12.4 kHz with amplitude 0.25, and these two tones must carry at least 99 % of the power; the lower sideband (the tones at 9.3 kHz and 7.6 kHz) and the carrier (10 kHz) must each be at least 30 dB weaker than the 12.4 kHz tone. In audio.dat the 700 Hz and 2.4 kHz tones must have the amplitudes given above. Tolerances: frequencies within 1 %, amplitudes within 5 %. Everything is measured from 0.1 s after the start, so filter start-up does not count. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.
observation: the float samples written to the File Sink whose file name is audio.dat (the 8 kHz two-tone audio) and the float samples written to the File Sink whose file name is ssb.dat (the 48 kHz USB signal)

known_limits: Version 2: re-themed in the round-1 fix stage (version 1, a two-channel DDC, was a cross-split twin of gbf-test-18; resolution in reports/tier_f_reviews/round1/gbf-dev-06.resolution.json). Composed L2 item: the approved plan says L2 tasks come from converted examples and eval plan 4.3 lists only hand-written L1 chains, so composed L2 items need the team's sign-off (fix_plan team_decisions; only L3 seeds remain unused in dev). The upper test tone is 2.4 kHz, not the 1.9 kHz of the classic two-tone test, so that a zero-order-hold (Repeat) interpolator, whose droop violates the 5 % amplitude tolerance, is rejected (at 1.9 kHz it passed). Known oracle limits: (1) the Hilbert requirement is checked structurally (a Hilbert block on a source -> File Sink path); a contrived graph that adds a Hilbert block on a side branch to another File Sink and makes ssb.dat some other way would pass. (2) Only GNU Radio's Hilbert block (hilbert_fc) counts, as the instruction names it. Two other Hilbert-transformer constructions fail the graph check: the Filter Delay block (filter_delay_fc) with firdes.hilbert taps, and an FIR filter with firdes.hilbert taps plus a matching Delay. Team decision: keep the block named, or drop the structural requirement. Dropping it would also admit the filter and Weaver methods, whose v2 cell is gbf-test-18's test cell. The FIR + Delay form hashes to train (combine|delay|filter|hilbert|mix|resample|tone). The Filter Delay form gets the unmapped class other:filter_delay_fc, which hashes to test. (3) The default 65-tap Hilbert placed at 48 kHz misses the stated 30 dB (about 16 dB below the 12.4 kHz tone); placing it at 8 kHz or giving it >= ~97 taps (Hamming) passes. (4) 'Made from the 8 kHz audio' is checked as a rate-increasing block on a path from a source to the block that shifts the signal to the carrier (Multiply, Multiply Conjugate, Rotator, Frequency Xlating filter, Embedded Python). A graph that generates the tones at 48 kHz, builds the SSB from them and decimates only the copy for audio.dat fails it, whichever decimator it uses (Rational Resampler, Low Pass Filter or Keep 1 in N). The check cannot read rate parameters, so a contrived graph that puts a 1:1 resampler or a non-interpolating Low Pass Filter between 48 kHz tones and the mixer would pass. (5) Amplitude tolerance: there is no per-band absolute power feature, so the oracle bounds each tone's share of the power and the total rms. This accepts every answer with both amplitudes within 5 %, but also some with one tone further off (up to about 8 % for the 700 Hz tone and 12 % for the 2.4 kHz tone).

instruction:
This flowgraph demonstrates time-division multiplexing of two streams of real 32-bit float samples. Two repeating Vector Sources produce stream A (1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11) and stream B (5, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14). A Stream Mux takes 4 samples from stream A, then 3 samples from stream B, and repeats, so after the Throttle the File Sink writing mux_out.dat receives 1, 2, 3, ..., 14, 1, 2, 3, ... as float samples. Two more File Sinks record the streams before multiplexing: stream A in stream_a.dat and stream B in stream_b.dat.

I want every 7-sample frame (the 4 samples from stream A followed by the 3 samples from stream B) to be preceded by a two-sample header: the value -1 followed by the value -2. The float samples written to mux_out.dat must therefore start with a header and read -1, -2, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, -1, -2, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, -1, -2, 1, 2, ..., repeating this 18-sample pattern exactly, with no sample missing, added or out of place. The frames must still be built from streams A and B by multiplexing (I will change the streams later), and the Throttle must stay in front of mux_out.dat. Keep streams A and B as they are: stream_a.dat and stream_b.dat must still receive them exactly as before, from their first sample. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.
observation: the float samples written to the File Sink whose file name is mux_out.dat, and the float samples written to the File Sinks stream_a.dat and stream_b.dat
oracle_checks: f2p:equal_prefix@out; p2p:equal_prefix@a; p2p:equal_prefix@b; p2p:graph:path; p2p:graph:path; p2p:graph:path
gates: PASS mutation=ok, size=ok, solvability=ok, start_fails=ok, variants=ok
known_limits: Known oracle limits: (1) 'the frames must still be built from streams A and B by multiplexing' is checked structurally: the Vector Source behind stream_a.dat, and the one behind stream_b.dat, must each reach the File Sink of mux_out.dat through one of the stream-merging blocks listed in build.py MERGERS (Embedded Python blocks included). This rejects a fixed output with or without a merging block (an Add with a zero source, the Stream Mux set to one input) and a header-baked copy of stream A multiplexed with stream B (probes x_hardcoded_*, x_doctored_copy_of_a). A deliberately contrived graph that still wires streams A and B into a merging block but takes the output values from elsewhere could pass; where the samples come from cannot be observed in a single run. Team decision (fix plan): keep this graph check or drop the sentence. (2) 'The Throttle must stay in front of mux_out.dat' is checked structurally only; its rate is not observable and not stated. (3) 'Keep producing samples until stopped' is checked only by V4 liveness (8192 items per observation point). (4) Stream tags (tag0 / tag1) are not checked. (5) Header-after-frame cannot be made by one mutation operator on this reference, so it is a probe (fails V5 f2p), not a gate mutant. Licence: derived from the GNU Radio 3.10.12 example blocks/stream_mux_demo.grc (author David Pi, GNU GPL 3.0+); the item keeps the GPL-3.0-or-later attribution (licence decision is the team's).

instruction:
This flowgraph demonstrates the effect of quantization. It runs at a sample rate of 48 kHz. A Noise Source produces noise with a standard deviation of 0.1 (-20 dB), which a band-pass filter limits to the band from 6 kHz to 18 kHz, and a Signal Source adds a 12.6 kHz tone with amplitude 0.316 (-10 dB); all samples are floats. The sum should then be quantized to 6 bits: every sample is rounded to the nearest multiple of 1/32 (= 1/2^(6-1)). The quantized signal must be written as float samples to the File Sink with file name quantized.dat, and the quantized signal multiplied by 32 (the integer quantization levels) must be written as float samples to the File Sink with file name codes.dat. Below 4 kHz and above 20 kHz, the spectrum of both outputs should show nothing but the flat noise floor that 6-bit rounding produces (power (1/32)^2/12 in quantized.dat).

At the moment the flowgraph cannot be generated: GNU Radio Companion shows the block named 'quantizer' as a Missing Block, with the error 'Block id "blocks_quantizer_ff" not found.' Please repair the flowgraph so that it works as described; the repaired flowgraph must not contain any Missing Block, not even a disabled one. Keep the sample rate, the noise level and its 6-18 kHz band, the tone, the 6-bit resolution and both output files as they are. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples. The outputs are judged after the first 512 samples: the tone frequency within 1 %, signal and noise levels within 5 %, the noise band's edges within about 0.1 kHz and the rounding-noise floor within about 0.6 dB.
observation: the float samples written to the File Sink whose file name is quantized.dat (the quantized signal) and to the File Sink whose file name is codes.dat (the quantized signal times 32), each after skipping the first 512 samples (filter start-up)
oracle_checks: f2p:max_int_dev@out; f2p:max_int_dev@codes; f2p:band_fraction@out; f2p:band_fraction@out; f2p:band_fraction@codes; f2p:band_fraction@codes; p2p:rms@codes; p2p:peak_freq@out; p2p:rms@out; p2p:band_fraction@out; p2p:band_fraction@out; p2p:band_fraction@out; p2p:band_fraction@out

known_limits: Revised 18 Oct after review round 1 (see reports/tier_f_reviews/round1/gbf-dev-08.resolution.json). The instruction states only what V5 checks: it no longer describes the filter's window and transition width, the noise as Gaussian, the tone as a cosine or the Throttle (none of them is observable at the outputs; the start graph shows them). The band edges are checked by the power within +-0.4 kHz of 6 and 18 kHz, which an edge moved by 0.1 kHz changes by ~15 % and by 0.2 kHz by 28-33 % (tolerance +-20 %), while the window and the transition width (1.2-4.8 kHz) change it by at most ~8 %. Known oracle limits: (1) a transition width above ~4.5 kHz fails because noise leaks below 4 kHz (the stated floor), narrower widths are free. (2) The noise seed is not part of the description; any seed passes (v4 uses seed 7). instruction:
This flowgraph simulates a burst BPSK link and its receiver. A Vector Source repeats one packet of bytes: the 8-byte preamble 0x2E 0xA4 0xAF 0x33 0x1F 0x22 0xF1 0xF7, then a 124-byte payload (4 zero bytes followed by the 120 pseudo-random bytes numpy.random.RandomState(7).randint(0, 256, 120)), sent most significant bit first. A Constellation Modulator turns each bit into one BPSK symbol (bit 0 -> +1, bit 1 -> -1, no differential coding) at 5 samples per symbol with root-raised-cosine pulses of excess bandwidth 0.4. A Stream Mux alternates 5,280 samples of the modulator's output (1,056 symbol periods) with 4,000 zero samples from a Null Source (800 symbol periods), so the receiver sees a burst of 1,056 symbols every 1,856 symbol periods. Because of the modulator's pulse-shaping delay, each burst after the first starts with the last 27 symbols of one packet, followed by the first 1,029 symbols of the next. After a Throttle (250,000 samples/s), a Channel Model adds a carrier frequency offset of 0.0005 cycles per sample (no noise, no timing offset). On the receive side a Correlation Estimator looks for the modulated preamble, a Polyphase Clock Sync recovers the symbol timing with a bank of matched root-raised-cosine filters and outputs one sample per symbol, and a Costas loop of order 2 removes the carrier offset.

The recovered symbols must be written as complex samples to the File Sink with file name symbols.dat, one sample per symbol. From the second burst on, every burst must reproduce the transmitted symbol stream: over the burst, the normalised correlation between the recovered symbols and the transmitted ±1 symbols must be at least 0.95, and so must the correlation over the 64 preamble symbols within it (a perfect receiver gives 1; a constant phase rotation, such as the 180-degree ambiguity of BPSK, and a fixed delay are fine). Between bursts the output must be silent: an RMS below 0.01 over the middle 500 of the 800 silent symbol periods. The Costas loop's frequency estimate (its second output) must be written as float samples to the File Sink with file name freq.dat; while a burst is being received, from its 300th to its 1,000th symbol, the estimate must average the carrier offset in radians per symbol, 2*pi*0.0005*5 = 0.0157, within 1 %. The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.

Please repair the flowgraph so that it validates, runs and behaves as described. Keep the transmitter (the modulator's output must stay exactly as it is), the burst timing, the channel and both output files as they are, and keep the order-2 Costas loop in the receive chain.

known_limits: Known oracle limits (drafted by Claude; for the team). (1) The design numbers are checked through the stated strip criteria, not tap by tap (300-seed calibration in build.py): cutoff shifts of about 100 Hz are borderline, 250 Hz shifts fail for every window and seed; transition widths up to about 550 Hz (Hann), 700 Hz (Hamming) or 800 Hz (Blackman, Kaiser) pass, a doubled width (1 kHz) fails for every window. Narrower transitions pass, as 'no more than 500 Hz' allows. A Bartlett window (firdes taps only; not offered by the Band Pass Filter block) at 500 Hz misses the stated skirt criterion. (2) Noise level and passband gain are checked jointly through the RMS window 0.69-0.80: amplitude 1 with gain 2 gives the same signal, and the window has to cover the 0.716-0.773 spread of valid window choices, so 5 % level errors are not reliably detected (10 % high and 15 % low are). (3) 'Gaussian' is checked on the noise source's noise_type parameter (GRC's writer exports every parameter, so the harness's final graph always carries it; the compact gate files keep it explicitly). (4) The path check proves that filtered noise reaches the File Sink; an answer that also adds tones on that path could pass. (5) The noise seed is not specified (any seed passes; the reference keeps seed 2718 so gate runs are bit-identical). (6) A Head block larger than the 65536-item capture is not detected (probe head_100000). (7) A rectangular-window Band Pass Filter with a 340-375 Hz transition has an expected RMS of 0.79-0.805 (its passband ripple raises the average gain about 4 %, because GNU Radio normalises the gain at the band centre), so it fails the stated RMS window on some or most seeds; widening the window would also admit a 10 % gain error (0.812-0.845). Its second (debug) output, the detector's running average of the input, must be written to the File Sink with file name average.dat and item type float; from 0.1 s after the start it should stay within 5 % of the sawtooth's average level of 1.0, between 0.95 and 1.05.

instruction:
This flowgraph simulates a QPSK link to demonstrate symbol timing recovery. It runs at a sample rate of 48 kHz. The transmitter takes random QPSK symbols (GNU Radio's QPSK constellation, points ±1.414 ± 1.414j, i.e. magnitude 2) and pulse-shapes them with root-raised-cosine filtering (roll-off 0.5) in a polyphase arbitrary resampler, at a symbol rate of 9.6 kBd; its output is written as complex items to the File Sink whose file name is tx_signal.dat. A channel model adds Gaussian noise (noise voltage 0.05) and a sample-clock offset of 0.2 % (timing offset 0.998, so the receiver sees about 0.2 % more samples per symbol than nominal), with no frequency offset. The receiver is a Polyphase Clock Sync whose bank of root-raised-cosine filters is matched to the transmitter's pulse and symbol rate. It should lock onto the symbol timing and output one sample per symbol, written as complex items to the File Sink whose file name is rx_symbols.dat; its timing error, rate and phase outputs go to the File Sinks timing_error.dat, timing_rate.dat and timing_phase.dat (float items).

Once the timing loop has settled, that is from the 2,049th recovered symbol on, the recovered symbols must be the transmitted symbol sequence, in order, without slipped or extra symbols and without any rotation or I/Q mirroring of the constellation (a fixed delay is fine): at the best fixed delay, their normalised correlation with the transmitted complex QPSK symbols must be at least 0.95. Each recovered symbol must sit on its QPSK point: none with a magnitude above 2.5, and an RMS magnitude of 2.0 (within 5 %). The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.
